label: Aquinas on willing a creature's esse and directing creatures to ends
summary: ST I q.20 a.2 co. derives willing a creature's esse to it on the basis of q.19 a.4's will as cause. Its ad 3 orders irrational creatures to rational creatures and God under quasi-desire. That reply does not assert the exclusive denial of willing a creature's esse to it, nor specify the typed esse-indexed ordering of 7f6a2e91 as a separate thesis. ST I q.22 aa.1–2 puts every creature, including each individual insofar as it participates in being, under the ordering of the universal first cause, with providence in intellect and presupposing a willed end. The chosen generic causation relations leave acting through will open in both routes. Follow-up (2026-11-26). The pinned I q.20 a.2 ad 3 specifies God’s ordering of irrational creatures to rational creatures and to himself. Q.19 a.5 co. and ad 1 supplies the distinction between willing an order of means to an end and being moved to will by that end. The combination leaves open the index on the act of willing in 7f6a2e91: willing esse to a subject in the body of q.20 a.2 and ordering the creature to another in ad 3 do not state a single esse-indexed ordering relation. A direct root route uses recipient-directed willing, while the weak ordered sibling is a comparison.
blocker: For love, test whether divine willing of a creature’s esse specifies its order in the same respect, while preserving compatibility with willing esse to the creature itself. For providence, keep the intellectual plan distinct from execution.
